On Mon, Jun 27, 2016 at 11:01 PM, Ed Merkle <ecme...@gmail.com> wrote:
> 1. General-purpose samplers like JAGS or BUGS will always be somewhat slow,
> sacrificing speed for flexibility. However, run times on the order of hours
> do seem extreme. I wonder whether you are running into memory issues
> associated with having lots of missing data (the missing data are generally
> sampled as extra parameters, and this is handled behind the scenes). I'd be
> interested if your setup is slow on the examples from the manual, using
> "jagcontrol=list(method='rjparallel')" if you have multiple cores. For
> example, I can complete the bsem() example in about 90 seconds.

Along with the missing data timings, I have been investigating the
political example, and there seems to be some serious problems with
the parallelism: parallelism leads to major slowdowns, not speedups!

Some background: my laptop exposes 8 cores. 1 core is used by Firefox,
1 core is used by Torch training a deep net (which pegs a CPU although
the GPU does most of the heavy lifting), which leaves 6 cores idle. My
currently installed blavaan still has the `n.chains=1` crash bug, so
for benchmarking I compare 2 chains/cores to the default of 3
chains/cores and my usual option of 6 chains/cores.

My belief was that since you say that blavaan collects a *total* of
_n_ samples rather than _n_ samples per chain, `n.chains=6` should
represent roughly a halving of wallclock runtime compared to the
default `n.chains=3`; even if you misunderstood your code and it's
collecting _n_ samples from each chain, it should still be similar
runtime since the penalty of setting up additional processes should be
no more than a few seconds and each MCMC process will run in similar
time on their own cores. Watching them in `top`, the expected number
of R processes appear and they take up ~100% of their own cores, as
expected, and blavaan doesn't issue any parallelism-related warnings
that I can see. So things look fine here and there should be a
speedup.

Instead, it seems that additional chains *increase* runtime and going
from 3 to 6 doubles wallclock time. Watching `bsem()` runs, the
doubling appears to hit during the main MCMC run and isn't due to,
say, the PPCs (which don't make much of a difference to the runtime)
or the summary statistics. And this increase also occurs going from
`n.chains=2` to the default `n.chains=3`.

(This is bad, but on the bright side, it also explains part of why my
blavaan runs take so long!)

---

General timing with the `bsem()` example, all times in seconds are
from the 'elapsed' return value of `system.time()`:

1. baseline example model & reduced parallelism (2 chains rather than
`bsem` default of 3): 50/57/45/45/44/46s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=2))
2. baseline example model & normal parallelism (3): 73/80/86/63/56/56s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel")))
3. baseline example model & high parallelism: 127/130/133/128/120/120s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=6))
4. baseline with n=100k & reduced parallelism: 267/306/301/252/261/291s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=2, sample=100000))
5. baseline with n=100k & normal parallelism: 414/399/419/405/337/370s:

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
sample=100000))
6. baseline with n=100k & high parallelism: 755/757/765/718/776/689s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=6, sample=100000))
7. baseline with n=100k & same options as my SEMs & reduced
parallelism: 271/270/285/275/247/584s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=2, sample=100000, test="none", fixed.x=FALSE))
8. baseline with n=100k & normal parallelism & same options as my
SEMs: 440/435/482/609/626/637s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
sample=100000, test="none", fixed.x=FALSE))
9. baseline with n=100k & same options as my SEMs & high parallelism:
868/932/779s

system.time(fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy,
dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"), jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
n.chains=6, sample=100000, test="none", fixed.x=FALSE))

Can anyone replicate these timings on their system?

I can replicate the increase in run time as we increase the number of chains. However, the "sample" argument is per chain (not total across chains), so that moving from 6 chains to 2 increases the number of samples drawn. Maybe this explains part of it.

blavaan simply calls run.jags() using the "rjparallel" option, so I'm not sure that I can modify anything here. The parallelism comes from runjags.

Ed

I will get to the system.time() calls slowly (upcoming conferences keeping me busy). As I think about it more, I think the slowdown comes from summarizing the extra samples. First, runjags calculates posterior means/sds/etc using all samples drawn. Second, blavaan calculates log-likelihoods for each sample drawn. Some if (maybe all) of these calculations are not parallel, which partly explains the time increase.

Ed

> drawn. Some if (maybe all) of these calculations are not parallel, which

Does blavaan do any of those calculations with burnin samples? (I
don't think anything needs to be done, they can be discarded as soon
as they're generated.) If not, then perhaps one work around for
parallelizing difficult models is to simply increase the burnin
substantially.

The burnin samples never make it out of JAGS, so you could indeed use large burnin and then summarize fewer samples following burnin. I also just wrote some code that uses mclapply() for the posterior summaries, so this should also speed things up a bit.

Ed
